speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) when will the Tripartite Advisory on Mental Health be published; and (b) whether the advisory can be expedited to provide better support to workers suffering from mental-health-related issues arising from the workplace.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It has a list of external resources that employers can consider engaging to provide support for their workers’ mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Employers can also initiate support for their workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For instance, supervisors can check in regularly with their workers, talk to them to find out if they are facing any problems and refer them to external help if needed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The prolonged telecommuting arrangements have blurred boundaries between the home and the office for many of our workers, especially our PMETs.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Many have told me that they now work increasingly long hours as emails, calls and WhatsApp messages have come in outside of their regular working hours.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Some shared that they now have Zoom work meetings in the night, which they never had before COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In fact, they told me that they had not even heard of Zoom before COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, the work from home arrangement today has changed the way we work and brought access to the office into the home.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I fully recognise the challenges some of our workers are facing with regard to the blurred lines between work hours and personal time.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, I can see where the Member is coming from, where clearer boundaries between work and personal time would be useful.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But the same time as well, we have to also recognise that this is something new.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think it originated in France, if I am not mistaken – the El Khomri law.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And many countries are still observing and seeing how this works out before we can consider it – whether it is feasible and open to legislation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I ask the Minister whether he can confirm that the tripartite guidelines or advisory will make clear that employers should not request for information on a person's mental health condition unless the condition has a direct connection with their ability to perform the job role.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think, today, the practice is already in place and something we encourage strongly.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this is something that we need to hold strong, too.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But look out for the advisory once it is out.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But rest assured that we are looking at various areas in which we want to make sure that the well-being of our workers is well protected, both from the physical health as well as mental health states.
